workflow-instructions.name: parallel-epic-execution
workflow-instructions.overview:
Execute an entire epic using parallel subagents with a SERIAL PIPELINE per story. Pipeline length depends on current story status - respects partially completed sprints.
Stories within a wave run in parallel, but each story completes its full lifecycle before the orchestrator merges it. This is NOT batched phases - it's parallel serial pipelines.
Key Principle: The SM orchestrator owns all git operations (branch creation, merging, pushing) and status updates. Dev subagents only commit within their branches.

pipeline-by-status.status: create → validate → implement → review (4 CLI calls)
SKIP - do not create worktree or dispatch

prerequisites.item: Clean git state on integration branch (dev)

step.title: Load Context
step.action: Read sprint-status.yaml to identify stories for the target epic
Read project_context.md for coding standards
Read implementation readiness report for dependency analysis (if exists)
Identify all stories with status: drafted, backlog, or ready-for-dev

step.title: Dependency Analysis
step.action: Map story dependencies within the epic
Identify stories that can run in parallel (no dependencies on pending stories)
Group stories into waves based on dependencies
step.output: Wave plan example: - Wave 1: Stories with no internal dependencies (can run parallel) - Wave 2: Stories depending on Wave 1 completion - Wave N: Final stories with most dependencies

step.title: Verify Prerequisites
step.action: Note story status from sprint-status.yaml - this determines pipeline length
Skip stories with status=done (already complete)
Check git status - must be clean on dev branch
Limit wave size to max_parallel_stories (default: 3)

phase.name: 2-execution
phase.title: Parallel Story Execution (Serial Pipeline Per Story)

step.title: Create Worktrees for Wave
step.critical: Each story gets its own worktree for filesystem isolation
step.action: For each story in current wave, create a worktree:
step.note: Worktrees allow parallel CLI subprocesses without git checkout conflicts

step.title: Dispatch Serial Pipelines (Parallel per Wave)
step.critical: Use PARALLEL Bash tool calls - one per story - all in single message
Pipeline length depends on story status - skip stories already done
step.action: For stories with status=backlog (no story file yet), dispatch full pipeline:
step.pattern:
Bash({ command: "cd /tmp/wt-story-{story_id} && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:sm
*create-story {story_id} #yolo' && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:sm
*validate-create-story {story_id} #yolo' && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:dev
*develop-story {story_id} #yolo' && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:dev
*code-review {story_id} #yolo'", timeout: 600000 })
step.action: For stories with status=drafted (story file exists, not validated), dispatch validation + implementation:
step.pattern:
Bash({ command: "cd /tmp/wt-story-{story_id} && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:sm
*validate-create-story {story_id} #yolo' && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:dev
*develop-story {story_id} #yolo' && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p '/bmad:bmm:agents:dev
*code-review {story_id} #yolo'", timeout: 600000 })
step.action: For stories with status=ready-for-dev (validated, ready to implement), dispatch implementation only:
For stories with status=done, skip entirely (do not create worktree or dispatch)
step.note: All Bash calls in a single message execute concurrently
SM waits for all to complete before proceeding to merge

step.title: Check Progress (Optional)
step.description: While waiting, SM can poll worktree git logs for progress
step.command: for wt in /tmp/wt-story-*; do echo "=== $wt ===" && git -C $wt log --oneline -5; done
step.note: This is optional - SM can simply wait for Bash calls to return

step.title: Evaluate Results
step.action: When all Bash calls return, check exit codes
For each story, determine if pipeline completed successfully
Stories with non-zero exit code: log as blocked, skip merge
Stories with zero exit code: ready for merge

step.title: Merge and Update (Sequential)
step.critical: Orchestrator performs all merges and status updates
step.action: For each successful story (sequential to avoid conflicts):

sequence.item: git checkout dev && git pull origin dev
git add . && git commit -m "chore: mark story {story_id} done"

step.conflict-handling:
If merge conflict on sprint-status.yaml: - Accept incoming (dev) version - Re-apply the single status change for this story - Commit the resolved merge
If code merge conflict: - HALT and report to user for manual resolution

step.title: Wave Completion
step.action: When all stories in current wave processed:
Report results: N succeeded, M blocked
Verify tests pass on dev branch (if test command configured)
If tests fail: HALT and report to user
If next wave exists: return to step 2.0
If final wave complete: proceed to phase 3

step.title: Final Verification
step.action: Verify all epic stories show status: done in sprint-status.yaml
Run full test suite on dev branch
Verify build succeeds

step.title: Update Epic Status
step.action: Update sprint-status.yaml: epic-{N} status → done
Commit and push the epic completion

step.title: Generate Execution Log
step.action: Create execution log in sprint_artifacts:
step.output-template:
# Parallel Epic Execution Log - Epic {epic_number} Date: {date}
## Execution Summary - Total Stories: N - Waves Executed: M - Total Time: (if tracked)
## Wave Details ### Wave 1 - Stories: [list] - Parallel Executions: N - Issues Found in Review: X - Issues Fixed: Y
### Wave N...
## Story Results | Story | Implementation | Review | Issues | Status | |-------|---------------|--------|--------|--------| | 1-3 | success | approved_with_fixes | 5 | done |
## Files Changed - Total files: N - [grouped by story]
## Lessons Learned - [Any blockers or issues encountered]

step.title: Recommend Retrospective
step.action: Inform user that epic-retrospective workflow is available
Suggest running retrospective to capture learnings

scenario.name: implementation-failure
scenario.condition: Dev subagent returns status: failed or blocked
scenario.action: Report blocked stories at wave completion
User decides: retry, skip, or halt epic

scenario.name: review-rejection
scenario.action: Option A: Re-dispatch implementation with fix instructions
Option B: Flag for manual intervention

scenario.name: merge-conflict
scenario.action: If sprint-status.yaml only: auto-resolve as described in step 2.4
If code conflict: halt and request manual resolution

scenario.name: test-failure-on-dev
scenario.condition: Tests fail after merge to dev
scenario.action: Options: revert merge, fix forward, or manual intervention

constraints.item: Never dispatch more than max_parallel_stories concurrently
Always run code review before merge (no exceptions)
Orchestrator owns ALL git operations to dev branch
Subagents work only on their story branches
Push to origin after each successful merge (fail-fast)
